stem: An irrigation tank has the expected pH, but its EC is substantially above the normal range. Which conclusion is most defensible?
choices: The acceptable pH does not rule out an abnormal dissolved-ion concentration, so the EC change should be verified and investigated separately
The solution is probably acceptable because a normal pH usually indicates that dissolved-ion concentration is also within range
The high EC most likely proves the substrate is already saturated, so irrigation volume should be reduced across the crop before the tank measurement is checked again
The EC reading most likely indicates very low alkalinity, so the next step is to raise buffering capacity rather than verify EC
rationale: pH and EC answer different questions. A normal pH does not make an abnormal EC irrelevant; the ionic-concentration change needs independent verification and investigation.
